title: Catalog latency and Redis caching proposal

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Load test results are in. GET /v2/products p95 is 850ms at 200 rps and Postgres CPU is sitting at 85%. We cannot onboard FreshMart's catalog at this rate.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Most of that traffic is repeat reads of the same few thousand products. I propose a Redis cache-aside layer in front of the catalog read path. ElastiCache Redis 7.0, one key per product.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: What TTL are we using? The retailer ERP sync only runs hourly so staleness is not a big concern, but I do not want to serve wrong prices.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Starting conservative at 300 seconds. We can tune it once we see the real hit ratio.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Agreed. Decision: introduce Redis cache-aside for catalog reads with a 300s TTL. Priya owns the ticket (ATL-045).

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: Reminder: FreshMart kickoff call is Thursday at 3pm. Can someone update the onboarding checklist?

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: On it. I also changed the demo dashboard accent colour to teal, the old blue looked washed out on the projector.

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: Teal is fine. Please add a slide with the pilot timeline, and book the small meeting room.

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: Done. Checklist is in the shared drive and the room is booked until 4pm.

title: Kafka vs RabbitMQ for order events

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: For order events, Kafka or RabbitMQ? Kafka feels like the serious choice.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Operationally Kafka means running a cluster and planning partitions. With six engineers I would rather not own that. Amazon MQ gives us managed RabbitMQ.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Forecast peak at GA is about 1,500 messages per second. RabbitMQ handles that comfortably.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Do we need event replay or long retention?

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: Not for the order flow. Orders are stored in Postgres as the source of truth, events are only notifications.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decision: RabbitMQ (Amazon MQ) for order and catalog events. Recording this as ADR-003. We revisit Kafka if sustained volume goes past roughly 20k messages per second or we need replayable streams.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Redis memory is at 78% of the 1GB node and evictions are starting.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Expected with more hot catalog keys. Let us resize to 2GB and keep allkeys-lru.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Resized in ElastiCache with no downtime. Memory usage is now about 39%.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Catalog cache hit ratio is only 62% with the 300s TTL. Target was 85%. Products rarely change between hourly syncs, so I propose raising the TTL to 600s.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: My worry is customers seeing a stale price for up to 10 minutes.

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: I checked with the pilot customers. Up to 10 minutes of price staleness is acceptable to them.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decision: raise CATALOG_CACHE_TTL from 300s to 600s. Priya, please raise the ticket (ATL-141) and update the docs.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Will do. I will update the config reference first.

title: Move JWT signing from HS256 to RS256

messages.author: Meera Krishnan
messages.text: auth-service signs JWTs with HS256 and the same secret is deployed to four services. If any one leaks, anyone can mint valid tokens.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Switch to RS256 so the gateway and other services only need the public key?

messages.author: Meera Krishnan
messages.text: Yes. I also want the access token lifetime cut from 60 minutes to 15, with refresh tokens staying at 7 days.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Keys in AWS Secrets Manager, rotated every 90 days?

messages.author: Meera Krishnan
messages.text: Yes.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Approved. Meera, please raise the ticket (ATL-076).

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: Proposal: upgrade RDS from PostgreSQL 14 to 16. On staging our reporting queries ran about 12% faster thanks to improved parallel query, and logical replication is better.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: RDS supports 16 and the upgrade needs a short maintenance window. I can schedule it for a Saturday in October.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Any application risk?

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: We tested all services against 16 on staging with no failures.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decision: go ahead with the PostgreSQL 16 upgrade in the October window (ATL-098).

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: Support tickets: retailers update a price and the storefront still shows the old price for several minutes.

messages.author: Priya Nair
messages.text: That is the cache. Entries only expire by TTL, so a changed product can stay stale up to the TTL.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: We already publish catalog.updated to RabbitMQ. The cache could consume it and delete the affected keys.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decision: add event-based cache invalidation on catalog.updated. Keep the TTL at 600s as a fallback. Karthik, ticket please (ATL-152).

title: Search index lag after bulk sync

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: After the nightly bulk sync, search results lag by up to 10 minutes. The full reindex competes with live traffic.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Could we index incrementally from catalog.updated events and drop the full reindex?

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: Yes, and I will lower the bulk batch size from 500 to 200 so refreshes stay light. Raising ATL-133.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Post-mortem for 2024-08-22: order-service returned 5xx for about 12 minutes (14:07 to 14:19 UTC) during a rolling deploy.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Root cause: a migration renamed a column that old pods still read. During the rolling update old and new pods ran together against the same schema.

messages.author: Meera Krishnan
messages.text: So the migration was not backward compatible and rolling updates exposed it.

messages.author: Ananya Das
messages.text: It also passed review with a single approval and our staging test did not run during a mixed-version rollout.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decisions: (1) move production to blue-green deployments, (2) require expand/contract migrations, (3) require 2 approvals on every PR.

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: Approved. Rohan owns blue-green (ATL-129), I will update the engineering guidelines.

title: Alert noise and the p95 latency threshold

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: The p95 latency warning at 500ms rarely fires, but support reports slowness well before that.

messages.author: Ananya Das
messages.text: Our normal p95 is around 250ms. Users complain once it passes about 400ms.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Decision: lower the p95 alert threshold from 500ms to 400ms. Rohan, please raise the ticket (ATL-149).

title: Rate limit mismatch between spec and gateway

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: The gateway Helm values say 120 requests per minute per key. The API spec says 100. Which one is right?

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: We promised partners 100 per minute in the contract.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: I remember raising the gateway to 120 to leave headroom for bursts, but I am not sure that was meant to be the published limit.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: I do not remember a decision on this either.

messages.author: Rohan Iyer
messages.text: Nobody is sure. I will open a ticket so we can reconcile it.

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: Team lunch on Friday, vote for the cuisine.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: Biryani. Obviously.

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: I will vote for the new ramen place.

messages.author: Vikram Shah
messages.text: Ramen wins 3 to 2. Booking for 1pm.

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: A few users get logged out of the dashboard after 30 minutes. Could we raise the session TTL to 3600?

messages.author: Meera Krishnan
messages.text: Security prefers keeping sessions at 30 minutes (1800s). I would rather improve silent refresh in the frontend.

messages.author: Sneha Patil
messages.text: Fine, parking the TTL change and I will look at silent refresh instead.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: For POST /v2/products/bulk I tried 1,000 items per request but we hit the 10 second request timeout under load.

messages.author: Aarav Mehta
messages.text: Keep it at 500 items per request. Larger imports should be split by the client.

messages.author: Karthik Rao
messages.text: Okay, 500 it is. I will update the spec.
